newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish confidence vote delayed as MPs fight.
newsitem.headline: Turkish confidence vote delayed as MPs fight.

text.p: A confidence vote in Turkey's new government degenerated into mayhem on Saturday when a secularist member of parliament denounced an Islamist rival as a "pimp" and demanded he leave the hall.
Deputies in the 550-seat assembly had cast just 30 votes when angry Islamist deputies rushed the podium and a fist fight broke out.
"I am calling a recess," speaker Mustafa Kalemli told the MPs amid shouts of anger. The vote was suspended for 15 minutes before deputies returned to their seats.

Parliament television's live broadcast went off the air and witnesses said a member of the Islam-based Welfare Party drew a pistol as the row spilled over into the corridors of parliament. No shots were fired.

The fighting began when a left-wing deputy unfurled a banner, reading "Get out, pimp," in a reference to Islamist firebrand Sevki Yilmaz who angered MPs of all hues with derogatory remarks broadcast on Turkish television last month.

Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz, no relation to the Islamist, was expected to win the vote in his secularist government, set up two weeks ago after former Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned.
